topics.label: Lecture framing: cancer hallmarks and loss of growth control
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic sets out the lecture’s place in the course, its aims, and its focus on cancer hallmarks rather than developing a specific hallmark mechanism.

topics.label: Extracellular signaling pathways that promote growth and survival
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in external-signal receptors and intracellular pathways can disrupt growth control by increasing proliferation or survival, or removing inhibitory signals.

topics.label: Differentiation blocks in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how impaired differentiation appears in blood cancers and intestinal epithelium, and how it can be recognized in the affected cells and tissues.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis through p53 and BCL2-family changes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how changes to p53, Bax, and BCL2 can prevent the cell from carrying out apoptosis.

topics.label: Replicative senescence, telomere maintenance, and growth-control safeguards
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how telomere shortening and stress responses normally limit continued cell proliferation, how TERT can help cancer cells bypass the replicative limit, and conclude the discussion of growth-control hallmarks.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolites in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer-associated changes in glucose use and metabolic pathways affect tumor cells and can interact with gene regulation and the epigenome.

topics.label: Angiogenesis in tumor growth
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumors recruit blood vessels to support their growth and how angiogenesis changes during tumor development.

topics.label: Metastatic dissemination, survival, and secondary growth
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics follow cancer cells from entry into circulation through their chances of survival and growth at secondary sites, including what can be learned from metastases.

topics.label: Lecture summary and close
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesizes the lecture’s point that different mutation routes can converge on shared cancer hallmarks, then closes the lecture and invites questions.
